flags.title: TennCare 1115 Waiver — More Restrictive Than Standard Medicaid
flags.summary: Tennessee operates Medicaid through TennCare, a Section 1115 waiver that is MORE RESTRICTIVE than standard Medicaid. Enrollment is capped and periodic enrollment freezes occur. Adults without children are generally NOT eligible. Verify current enrollment status before assuming Medicaid coverage. TennCare Connect: 855-259-0701 / tenncareconnect.tn.gov.

flags.title: TANF $185/Month — Lowest Cash Assistance in Registry
flags.summary: Tennessee TANF (Families First) provides only $185/month for a family of 3 — the lowest cash assistance amount in the entire registry. This is insufficient for any basic need. Supplement with SNAP, LIHEAP, and community resources immediately. Apply: tn.gov/humanservices.

flags.title: UI $275/Week Maximum — Lowest UI Benefit in Registry
flags.summary: Tennessee unemployment insurance maximum is $275/week — the lowest in the registry. Duration: up to 26 weeks. Appeal deadline: 15 days from mailing. Contact TN DOL&WD: 844-224-5818 / jobs4tn.gov.

flags.title: Memphis Deep Poverty — 24-27% Poverty Rate, Church Health Model
flags.summary: Memphis has 24-27% poverty rate with concentrated poverty in North Memphis, South Memphis, and Frayser. Church Health (founded by Dr. Scott Morris) provides healthcare for working uninsured adults — a model unique to Memphis. Church Health: 901-272-7170 / churchhealth.org. Memphis Area Legal Services: 901-523-8822 / malsi.org.

flags.title: Nashville Refugee Hub — Kurdish, Somali, Burmese, Congolese Communities
flags.summary: Nashville is one of the largest refugee resettlement cities in the US with significant Kurdish (largest Kurdish population in US), Somali, Burmese, and Congolese communities. Language access is critical. Tennessee Immigrant & Refugee Rights Coalition (TIRRC): 615-833-0384 / tirrc.org. Catholic Charities of TN: 615-352-3087.

flags.title: URLTA Patchwork — Not All Counties Have Adopted Tenant Protections
flags.summary: Tennessee's Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (URLTA) has NOT been adopted by all counties. Rural counties may have weaker tenant protections. Verify whether the client's county has adopted URLTA before advising on tenant rights. TN Fair Housing Council: 615-874-2344.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Tennessee Emergency Detention
flags.message: TN involuntary psychiatric hold law: Tennessee Emergency Detention. Statutory authority: Tenn. Code § 33-6-401. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in TN retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in TN: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Tennessee Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Tennessee Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
